requirement.part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip

brief:
Part: cantilever bracket, load at the tip. Solid rectangular cross-section, width across the load, thickness in the load direction.
Load 2500 N at the tip, length 140 mm.
REQ-001 yield margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.25 (MS = allowable / (factor x stress) - 1).
REQ-002 ultimate margin of safety >= 0 with factor 1.6.
REQ-003 tip deflection <= 3 mm.
REQ-004 width 10-60 mm, thickness 3-30 mm.
REQ-005 thickness must be a stock plate thickness: [3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 30] mm.
REQ-006 REQ-001 to REQ-003 must still hold with the load 10% higher and the plate 0.5 mm thinner.
REQ-007 thickness / width <= 2 (a proxy for lateral stability).
Materials: {"Al 6061-T6": {"density_kg_m3": 2700, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 68.9, "yield_mpa": 276.0, "ultimate_mpa": 310.0}, "Ti-6Al-4V": {"density_kg_m3": 4430, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 113.8, "yield_mpa": 880.0, "ultimate_mpa": 950.0}, "Steel 4130": {"density_kg_m3": 7850, "youngs_modulus_gpa": 205.0, "yield_mpa": 435.0, "ultimate_mpa": 670.0}}
Goal: the lowest mass that meets every requirement.

reasoning:
Cantilever with tip load P=2500 N, L=140 mm. Rectangular section b (width) x t (thickness, bending direction). Bending stress sigma = 6PL/(b t^2). Shear is minor. Deflection = PL^3/(3EI), I = b t^3/12, so delta = 4PL^3/(E b t^3).

Stress checks: yield MS: allowable/(1.25 sigma) - 1 >= 0 -> sigma <= sigma_y/1.25. Ultimate: sigma <= sigma_u/1.6.
Robustness case (REQ-006): P=2750 N, t reduced 0.5 mm.

Stiffness governs for Al and maybe Steel given E. Ti has high yield, so strength is less limiting; stiffness (low E) drives thickness. Steel has high E so deflection is easy; strength governs, with yield allowable 348 MPa and ultimate allowable 419 MPa.

Notes should be per material on where to search. Mass = rho*b*t*L_length (length of bracket unknown; mass per unit length proportional to rho*b*t). Lowest mass is min rho*b*t, subject to constraints.

Al: E=68.9 GPa is low, so deflection of 3 mm is the binding constraint, pushing thickness up; search the upper t range with minimal b.
Ti: strength is high (yield allowable 704 MPa), so deflection with E=113.8 GPa is likely the limit; search moderate t with b at minimum needed.
Steel: E=205 GPa makes deflection easy; strength (ultimate allowable 419 MPa, yield allowable 348 MPa) and density 7850 push toward thin-wide section; search lower t values near the minimum.

Let me quickly check Al: need delta = 4PL^3/(E b t^3) <= 3 mm with robustness case P=2750, t-0.5. Let's just write the notes and let specialists run physics checks.


<invoke name="Plan">
<parameter name="reasoning">Bending stress sigma = 6PL/(b t^2) and tip deflection delta = 4PL^3/(E b t^3), with P = 2500 N and L = 140 mm. REQ-006 (P = 2750 N, t 0.5 mm thinner) is the governing robustness case. Yield allowable = 276/1.25 = 220.8 MPa for Al, 880/1.25 = 704 MPa for Ti, 435/1.25 = 348 MPa for steel. Ultimate allowable = sigma_u/1.6 = 193.75, 593.75, 418.75 MPa. Mass per unit bracket length is proportional to rho*b*t, so the search minimises rho*b*t under these limits, with t restricted to the stock list and t/b <= 2.

Specialist notes are below. Each note gives the region to search and the reason.

notes.Al 6061-T6: Stiffness will likely govern because E is only 68.9 GPa, so the 3 mm deflection limit pushes t upward. Search the upper stock thicknesses (about 10-30 mm) with the smallest width that keeps t/b <= 2, and check the 2750 N / 0.5 mm thinner case.
notes.Ti-6Al-4V: Strength is not the constraint here (yield allowable about 704 MPa, ultimate about 594 MPa), so the search should focus on deflection with E = 113.8 GPa. Look at moderate thicknesses (around 6-12 mm) with the minimum width that meets the 3 mm deflection, and keep t/b <= 2.
notes.Steel 4130: E = 205 GPa makes deflection easy, so strength governs (yield allowable 348 MPa, ultimate allowable 419 MPa) and the 7850 kg/m^3 density penalises mass. Search the lower stock thicknesses (about 3-8 mm) with width set by the bending-stress limit, and check t/b <= 2.

text: Before checking, I estimated the sizing by hand. With M = PL = 350 N·m, the ultimate-strength margin (310/1.6 = 194 MPa) is tighter than the yield margin (276/1.25 = 221 MPa). Stiffness is the other constraint. Under the 2750 N / 0.5 mm-thinner case, the thickness-to-width limit and the stress limit together push toward thick, narrow sections. I'll check three candidates first.
I'll start with three candidates across the thickness range: a thin plate, a mid-thickness plate, and a thick plate.
The first three candidates all pass. The 15×30 mm design is the lightest so far. I'll check one more, a wider and thinner section, to round out the set.
The three candidates pass, and the mass numbers match my hand calculation. Thicker and narrower gives less mass, so next I'll check the 25 mm plate at a few widths.
I'll start with three Ti-6Al-4V candidates that bracket the expected lightest region: a 20 mm plate at 12 mm width, a 16 mm plate at 20 mm, and a 25 mm plate at 13 mm.
The 12.5 × 25 mm plate is the lightest so far at 343 g. Before proposing, I'll check whether a 20 mm plate can go narrower than my 18 mm candidate.

All four Al 6061-T6 designs pass every requirement, including the REQ-006 case (2750 N and 0.5 mm thinner). The lightest is 15 × 30 mm at 170 g. My hand estimates matched the tool's nominal values.

**Design A: 15 mm wide × 30 mm thick (lightest, 170.1 g)**
- Yield MS: +0.42 (my estimate 0.42)
- Tip deflection: 0.98 mm (my estimate 0.98 mm)
- Mass: 170.1 g
- Notes: t/w = 2.00, right at the REQ-007

The 20 × 12 mm design passes every requirement at 148.8 g. The 16 × 20 mm design fails REQ-006 (worst-case deflection 3.56 mm), so I'll drop it. To fill out the proposal set, I'll check a few other passing sizes near the minimum.

The lightest passing Steel 4130 design is a 12.5 mm × 25 mm plate at about 343 g. I checked 8 designs in total; the two 10 mm and 17.5 mm candidates at 20 mm thickness were added to confirm the width limit.

**Proposals (all checked, all pass every requirement):**

| # | Width × thickness (mm) | Yield MS (nominal) | Tip deflection (mm) | Mass (g) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12.5 × 25 | +0.29 | 0

I ran 6 Ti-6Al-4V checks. Four designs pass every requirement, and the 20 × 12 mm plate is the lightest. Yield margins use the 880 MPa yield with factor 1.25, which the tool confirmed.

| Design (w × t, mm) | Yield MS (nominal) | Tip deflection (mm) | Mass (g) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **12 × 20 (lightest)** | +0.61 | 2.51 | 148.8 |
| 13 × 20 | +0.74 | 2.32 | 161.3 |
| 14 × 20 | +0.88 | 2.15 | 173.7 |
